newsitem.title: UK: London gold, silver prices attempt foray higher.
newsitem.headline: London gold, silver prices attempt foray higher.

text.p: Gold and silver prices notched higher on Tuesday afternoon, bolstered by news of a wider than expected U.S. trade gap in September, dealers said.
But both metals foundered after meeting stiff resistance levels just overhead, dealers said.
Gold popped up to a high so far of $379.55 an ounce before easing back to fix at $379.10, up $0.50 from the morning fixing.
The absence of producer selling, which has helped depress prices since late last week, also contributed to gold's rise.
"The professional market was expecting gold to stay in the mid-$378 area. When it didn't they were caught on the short side and had to cover," one dealer said.
Costly oil imports and weak overseas sales of commerical aircraft helped the U.S. trade deficit to climb 10.1 percent to $11.34 billion from a revised $10.3 billion in August.

Economists had expected a narrowing in the trade gap to $9.5 billion. The surprisingly wide gap sent the dollar tumbling against the other major currencies, as forecasters predicted a downward revision of the U.S. gross domestic product.
But gold's upside potential was limited, dealers said.
"I don't think it's going to fly up much beyond $380," one said. Afternoon trading was fairly busy with decent volumes.
Analysts had forecast a slight bounce in gold due to its recent staying power above the critical price level just above $377 an ounce.
Next week's expiry of over-the-counter options, which provide the right but not the obligation to buy or sell metal at a given "strike" price, may also help push up prices.
"It's a week till the OTC options expiry and there's some interest at $380, and so I wouldn't be suprised if we edge up towards there," a dealer said.
Overall, however, market sentiment remained bearish since last week's rally, which peaked just under $385, reversed amid heavy selling from gold producers and investment funds.
Silver followed gold up to a high of $4.98/$5.00 an ounce, an advance of 10 cents from Tuesday's London close.
"Above $5 there's going to be a lot of stop loss buying, but there's a lot of resistance below there," a dealer said.

Silver had more potential than gold to move higher due to less selling pressure and stronger price charts, analysts said. Platinum was indicated up $0.25 at $383.75/$384.75, while palladium was virtually unchanged at $118.00/$119.00.
